response.text:
Recent work supports text-informed sequential recommendation, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of GRU4Rec, corpus-only text learning, and semantic hard negatives. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) represents items as attribute-text sentences and learns sequential retrieval through pretraining and finetuning; its Transformer backbone is outside this experiment’s family constraint. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) learns item-text representations through masked representation prediction and reports benefits in low-resource settings, but likewise uses a Transformer and two-stage training. These are architectural inspiration, not direct evidence that a small text encoder trained from scratch will improve GRU4Rec.

A compatible experimental hypothesis: randomly initialized token embeddings, title/description pooling or a small CNN, and a learned projection jointly integrated with item-ID embeddings inside one GRU network. Shared lexical parameters could help sparse items express purpose, artist, franchise, or product relationships; this remains an inference requiring validation. For sampling, [GNNO (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10047) mines hard negatives through item-graph neighborhood overlap, demonstrating an interaction-derived alternative to external semantic models. [R2NS (2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) investigates negative recall and reranking for sequential recommendation. A conservative adaptation would mix random negatives with moderately similar title/description candidates, exclude known training positives, and tune hardness cautiously: similarity can identify plausible positives as well as useful negatives. Compare text integration and sampling separately using the fixed macro validation HR@10; retain one jointly trained GRU checkpoint per category.
